title: Conjunction & Negation in Event Semantics (§11.5–11.6)
subtitle: The event-predicate fragment of §11.3, applied to VP coordination and sentential negation, with the diagnostics that motivate the continuation approach.

constants.e: f s g n a b l m o w sp

exercises.title: A. VP conjunction with one shared event
exercises.instructions: On the event-predicate approach (§11.3) a VP is a set of events ⟨v,t⟩. Conjunction follows the Partee & Rooth schema at that type: andVP ↝ λQ.λP.λe.[P(e) ∧ Q(e)], type ⟨⟨v,t⟩,⟨⟨v,t⟩,⟨v,t⟩⟩⟩. The Coord head applies to the right conjunct by FA, then to the left conjunct by FA, giving one event predicate. The Agent head joins by Predicate Modification and Existential Closure binds the single event. The prediction is one event that is both a smoking and a drinking.

exercises.title: B. The single-event prediction
exercises.instructions: Add a manner adverb to each conjunct. The single-event entry forces both predicates onto the same event, so the derivation makes one event both slow and quick. This is the textbook's argument (Exercise 3) that VP-and cannot denote a single shared event; the continuation fragment of §11.4 hands each conjunct its own event quantifier.

items.sentence: Frodo smoked slowly and drank quickly.
items.tree: [.S [.AgentP [.Agent Agent ] [.DP Frodo ] ] [.VP [.VP [.AdvP slowly ] [.VP smokeE ] ] [.CoordP [.Coord andVP ] [.VP [.AdvP quickly ] [.VP drinkE ] ] ] ] ]
items.note: One event e is forced to be both slow and quick. The continuation approach derives a two-event reading instead (§11.4, group E).

exercises.title: C. VP-internal negation
exercises.instructions: notVP ↝ λP.λe.¬P(e), type ⟨⟨v,t⟩,⟨v,t⟩⟩, maps the verb's event set to its complement. The Agent head then joins by Predicate Modification and Existential Closure binds the event. The result asserts only that some event by the subject is not a barking, true whenever Spot did anything besides barking. The textbook rejects this reading (tree 70).

items.note: Too weak: true whenever Spot does anything that is not a barking.
Same problem: any non-singing event by Frodo verifies it.

exercises.title: D. Negation above the event quantifier
exercises.instructions: The attested reading needs negation to scope above the existential event quantifier. Build the clause down to an event predicate ⟨v,t⟩, with the Agent joining by Predicate Modification; apply Existential Closure first to reach a truth value ∃e[…], and only then apply sentential negation not ↝ λp.¬p by Function Application. The result, ¬∃e[…], says there is no such event, which is what "Spot didn't bark" means.
